title: Drill Dozer
subtitle: A small pilot brings a very large drill
summary: Drill Dozer is Game Freak's Game Boy Advance action platformer starring Jill and the mechanical vehicle she pilots. Its drill turns in either direction, allowing the same central tool to break surfaces, engage enemies and operate objects in the surrounding levels. The cartridge contains a rumble motor that responds while drilling, giving the action a physical presence in the handheld. Rather than supplying a collection of unrelated weapons, the game builds its stages around discovering what this one machine can grip, pierce or turn as Jill searches for a route through the next obstacle.
body: Drill Dozer is Game Freak's Game Boy Advance action platformer starring Jill and the mechanical vehicle she pilots. Its drill turns in either direction, allowing the same central tool to break surfaces, engage enemies and operate objects in the surrounding levels. The cartridge contains a rumble motor that responds while drilling, giving the action a physical presence in the handheld. Rather than supplying a collection of unrelated weapons, the game builds its stages around discovering what this one machine can grip, pierce or turn as Jill searches for a route through the next obstacle.

Sprockets found during a stage unlock higher gears, allowing the drill to continue longer and break more resistant blocks. Shifting at the appropriate moment keeps the action going, making sustained drilling a sequence to manage rather than simply holding a button indefinitely. The upgrades reset between stages, giving each new area its own process of building the machine back toward full capability. The player therefore reads an obstacle in relation to the gear currently available, recognising when another sprocket is needed before a promising route can actually be forced open.

The two shoulder buttons control opposite drilling directions, allowing the machine to interact with screws and mechanisms as well as ordinary breakable surfaces. Shops provide health improvements, drill bits and maps leading to extra stages, giving collected currency a use between expeditions. Special sections can alter how the Dozer moves, but the drill remains the reference point for solving the next problem. Its flexible use gives Jill's machine a consistent physical identity, while the rumble inside the cartridge reinforces the sensation that the same piece of equipment is working against something solid on the screen.

Direction matters as much as strength
